name: Simulated Clinical Trials
title: Simulated Clinical Trials
answer: Simulated clinical trials use computational models to predict how a drug or device would perform in a human population before, or instead of, running a full physical trial. They draw on virtual patient cohorts, disease progression models, and trial protocol simulations to estimate efficacy, safety, and subgroup effects. In drug discovery and molecular simulation, this work sits between preclinical molecular modeling and later-stage human studies, often informing dose selection, endpoint choice, and go/no-go decisions. The goal is to reduce costly failures by testing hypotheses in silico first.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Simulated clinical trials use computational models to predict how a drug or device would perform in a human population before, or instead of, running a full physical trial. They draw on virtual patient cohorts, disease progression models, and trial protocol simulations to estimate efficacy, safety, and subgroup effects. In drug discovery and molecular simulation, this work sits between preclinical molecular modeling and later-stage human studies, often informing dose selection, endpoint choice, and go/no-go decisions. The goal is to reduce costly failures by testing hypotheses in silico first.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: These simulations run on high-performance computing clusters and cloud GPU instances, with storage for large patient-level datasets and model outputs. Inputs typically include electronic health records, genomic and biomarker data, pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic models, and historical trial results. The infrastructure must support reproducible pipelines, versioned model artifacts, and secure handling of de-identified or synthetic patient data. Many groups use containerized workflows and batch schedulers to run thousands of virtual trial scenarios.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The work combines mechanistic models, such as physiologically based pharmacokinetic models, with statistical and machine learning surrogates that emulate trial outcomes. Researchers build virtual patient populations by sampling from real or synthetic covariate distributions, then simulate disease progression and treatment response under a trial protocol. Models are calibrated against historical clinical data and validated on held-out trials or external registries. Common techniques include agent-based simulation, quantitative systems pharmacology, and Bayesian borrowing from prior studies.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Rights and risk center on data provenance, patient privacy, and the validity of simulation assumptions. Because simulated trials rely on historical patient data, consent, de-identification, and data use agreements must be clear, and synthetic data must not leak identifiable records. Regulatory acceptance is still developing, so sponsors must document model limitations, calibration evidence, and sensitivity analyses. The site tracks 210 compliance and regulation pages and 6 active product liability and wrongful death lawsuits against AI companies, reflecting the stakes when simulated evidence informs real clinical decisions.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Simulated trials are moving toward tighter integration with real-world evidence, adaptive trial designs, and digital twin approaches that update a virtual patient as new data arrive. Regulatory bodies are exploring qualification pathways for in silico evidence, though full replacement of human trials remains unlikely for most indications. The next few years will likely bring more standardized reporting, shared benchmark datasets, and hybrid designs where simulation narrows the question a physical trial must answer.
